entries.test: Public evaluations comparing performance on known prompts addressed through memorization or augmentation with performance on novel compositional tasks would test whether those fixes generalize.
entries.note: “Doesn’t mean” denies that success establishes a general solution; “does not indicate” more strongly denies its evidential relevance.

entries.test: Published evaluations documenting numerous AI techniques that solve targeted problems but fail on closely related problems would test this claim.
entries.note: The Band-Aid metaphor has a plain factual reading about limited generalization.

entries.test: Timestamped testing records showing Marcus eliciting numerous GPT-4o compositionality failures within a few minutes would settle the report.
entries.note: This describes failures in his testing, not a failure rate across all compositional tasks.

entries.test: The generated images and GPT-4o’s accompanying self-assessments would show whether it misidentified its own errors.
Public ARC-AGI-2 scores and results on its compositionality tasks available at publication would show how poorly contemporary systems performed.
entries.note: The normalized proposition omits “from what I understand,” making the assertion less qualified.

entries.test: Outputs from Marcus’s informal comparisons of GPT-4o and DALL-E 2 on compositional prompts would show whether GPT-4o performed markedly better.
entries.note: The comparison is explicitly limited to his informal testing.
He judges a particular inference unreasonable. Saying mastery “has not been shown” additionally rules out other possible evidence.
He raises potential training contamination rather than asserting that these prompts were in the training data.

entries.test: Comparative GPT-4o results on previously publicized prompts and comparable previously undiscussed prompts would test the asserted performance gap.
entries.note: The performance comparison is firm; the inference about robustness is qualified as a suggestion.
The central assertion judges the inference unjustified; it is not merely empty rhetoric. He separately endorses success on some compositionality problems.

entries.test: Timestamped records of Marcus’s session and six generated outputs would show whether he found six clear compositionality failures in under an hour.
entries.note: The normalization changes a report of what Marcus actually did into a statement about what could be done.
“Really at AGI” supplies no shared criterion for establishing the antecedent independently of the predicted improvement.

entries.test: Public testing at the end of 2027 would show whether clear compositionality failures remain readily elicitable in contemporary LLM-based generators, with comparative technical evidence testing the attribution to inherent LLM limitations.
entries.note: The preceding six failures in under an hour provide context for “easy to find.” The reference to inherent limitations is a causal explanation, not a conditional antecedent.
